A NEW LOOK. THE SAME PASSION. 20 SEASONS STRONG.

As we prepare to celebrate our 20th season of covering Utah High School Sports in 2027, we're excited to unveil a bold new look that represents who we are and where we want to be.

This new identity is a tribute to the pride we have in our state, and the countless athletes and programs that have made Utah High School Sports what they are today.

Over the past two decades, we've witnessed an incredible evolution. Utah's athletes, coaches, schools, and programs have elevated the level of competition, transforming our state into a hotbed of elite talent that is making waves on regional, national, and professional stages.

We're incredibly grateful to the countless student-athletes, coaches, families, and programs who have allowed us to be part of their journeys. It's been a privilege to share their stories, celebrate their accomplishments, and provide a platform where their talents can be recognized beyond the field or court.

Knowing that some of those spotlights we shined have helped athletes gain recognition and pursue their dreams of competing at the next level makes this journey even more meaningful. We're honored to have been a small part of so many incredible stories.

We're also incredibly proud of the talented broadcasters and media professionals who have been part of our team over the years. Many have gone on to incredible opportunities with the biggest names in sports media and knowing we've played a role in developing and showcasing the next generation of sports media talent has been amazing to be a part of.

To everyone who has been part of this journey over the last 19 seasons — thank you. You've helped build something we're incredibly proud of.

2027 marks 20 seasons. A new era. A new look. The same commitment to Utah High School Sports.

And we're just getting started.

WILD: Legendary #NFL WR Randy Moss was expelled from high school in 1995 after getting into a fight with another student.

Moss was one of the top recruits in the country and had committed to Notre Dame, but the school withdrew his scholarship following his arrest.

He eventually enrolled at Florida State, where he was dismissed from the football program after violating probation by testing positive for marijuana.

Moss transferred to Marshall, dominated college football, and went on to become one of the greatest wide receivers in NFL history.

ONE HELL OF A COMEBACK STORY.

text:
**James Chapter 2 (King James Version)**

1 My brethren, have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons.

2 For if there come unto your assembly a man with a gold ring, in goodly apparel, and there come in also a poor man in vile raiment;

3 And ye have respect to him that weareth the gay clothing, and say unto him, Sit thou here in a good place; and say to the poor, Stand thou there, or sit here under my footstool:

4 Are ye not then partial in yourselves, and are become judges of evil thoughts?

5 Hearken, my beloved brethren, Hath not God chosen the poor of this world rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which he hath promised to them that love him?

6 But ye have despised the poor. Do not rich men oppress you, and draw you before the judgment seats?

7 Do not they blaspheme that worthy name by the which ye are called?

8 If ye fulfil the royal law according to the scripture, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself, ye do well:

9 But if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors.

10 For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all.

11 For he that said, Do not commit adultery, said also, Do not kill. Now if thou commit no adultery, yet if thou kill, thou art become a transgressor of the law.

12 So speak ye, and so do, as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty.

13 For he shall have judgment without mercy, that hath shewed no mercy; and mercy rejoiceth against judgment.

14 What doth it profit, my brethren, though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? can faith save him?

15 If a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food,

16 And one of you say unto them, Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled; notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body; what doth it profit?

17 Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.

18 Yea, a man may say, Thou hast faith, and I have works: shew me thy faith without thy works, and I will shew thee my faith by my works.

19 Thou believest that there is one God; thou doest well: the devils also believe, and tremble.

20 But wilt thou know, O vain man, that faith without works is dead?

21 Was not Abraham our father justified by works, when he had offered Isaac his son upon the altar?

22 Seest thou how faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect?

23 And the scripture was fulfilled which saith, Abraham believed God, and it was imputed unto him for righteousness: and he was called the Friend of God.

24 Ye see then how that by works a man is justified, and not by faith only.

25 Likewise also was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers, and had sent them out another way?

26 For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead.

 King James Version (1611).

text:
Trump: US-PH ties closer than ever, cites bond with Marcos

By Darryl John Esguerra

MANILA – United States President Donald Trump on Tuesday described Washington’s current bilateral relations with Manila as “closer than ever,” crediting his personal relationship with President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. for strengthening the longstanding alliance.

Speaking at the ASEAN-US Special Summit in Manila, Trump said the two countries had significantly increased their defense cooperation, citing plans to expand joint Special Forces training and work together on defense modernization.

“But I don't think we've ever been closer than we are right now because of our personal relationship,” Trump said.

He described the Philippines as a key US ally and reiterated Washington’s commitment to supporting its partners across Southeast Asia and the Indo-Pacific.

The Philippines and the US are treaty allies and are marking 80 years of diplomatic relations this year, while ASEAN and the US will celebrate the 50th anniversary of their dialogue relations in 2027.

“We support our partners and our allies 100 percent. And when there's a problem, you call me,” Trump told the ASEAN leaders.

He also praised Marcos for his leadership as this year’s ASEAN chair and thanked him for hosting the special ASEAN-US summit, saying he had “done a good job.”

The Philippines has just concluded its rotational chairship of ASEAN. 
Trump is set to visit Malacañang on Wednesday and will hold a bilateral meeting with Marcos. 

The visit is Trump’s first stop on a three-day trip that will also take him to Shenzhen for a historic three-way nuclear talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit. 

According to Trump, a meeting with North Korea’s leader Kim Jong Un is also possible. 

Marcos is also set to fly to Shenzhen for the APEC Summit. (PNA)

POTUS IN MANILA. United States President Donald Trump waves American and Philippine flags as he descends the stairs from Air Force One upon arrival in Manila on Tuesday (Nov. 17, 2026). Trump is in the Philippines for the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits and bilateral talks with President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. (Photo courtesy of ASEAN PH 2026)

text:
GOV ENO DONATES CAR, BUSES TO AKWA IBOM STUDENTS 

Akwa Ibom State Governor, Pastor Umo Eno, has donated three buses to the students community in the state, alongside a brand new car to the President of the National Association of Akwa Ibom State Students (NAAKISS), Comrade Torobong Obot, as part of efforts to enhance students' welfare and ease their transportation challenges.

The donations were made during the 2026 International Students Day Celebration held on Tuesday, November 17, at the Uyo Township Stadium.

The three buses are designated for students across the state's three senatorial districts, while the car was presented to the NAAKISS President in recognition of the association's leadership.

Governor Eno also assured the students  that his administration would continue to support their welfare, academic pursuits and activities across tertiary institutions in the state. 

He urged them to remain focused on their studies, describing them as the future of Akwa Ibom State and Nigeria.

Speaking on behalf of the students, the Vice President, Special Duties of the National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS), Comrade Dominic Ernest, applauded Governor Eno for what he described as unprecedented achievements in the education sector and his administration's commitment to students' welfare.

Ernest described Governor Eno as the best students-friendly Governor, noting that International Students Day, which was traditionally an occasion for students to lament their challenges, had become a celebration of the Governor's interventions. He particularly commended the increase in students' bursary from N20,000 to N50,000, with a planned further increase to N200,000 and N250,000 for students studying Medicine, Law and Engineering in 2027.

The student leader also appreciated President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for introducing the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), which he said had helped students finance their education, as well as his efforts towards sustaining industrial peace in public institutions. 

Following motions moved by the NAAKISS President, Comrade Torobong Obot, and seconded by the Chairman of G-31, Comrade Anietie Samuel, the students unanimously endorsed the re-election of President Tinubu, Senate President Godswill Akpabio, Governor Umo Eno and all candidates of the All Progressives Congress (APC).

Earlier, the Governor's Special Assistant on Student Affairs, Dr. Wisdom Emmanuel, described Eno as a leader who places premium on students' welfare, adding that the celebration provided an opportunity for students to appreciate his administration's interventions and reaffirm their confidence in his vision for their future.

Responding, Governor Eno thanked the students for the recognition and their endorsement, and explained that the planned increase in bursary was intended to enable students meet their tuition obligations, reduce the financial burden on parents and allow them to concentrate on their studies. .

He reiterated his administration's commitment to improving educational standards through the declaration of a state of emergency in the sector and the establishment of an implementation committee chaired by the Deputy Governor, Senator Akon Eyakenyi.

Nope.  Look it up, if you can.  Here's some more from the Qur'an.  I know it's a lot of words and all...some big words.  I am included summaries so you can understand what it all means.  At the end, I actually quote some of Muhammad's own words, you should be able to understand those.  The Qur'an:

- Mandates fighting and killing those who fight against the believers, expelling enemies from their land, and continuing warfare until all persecution ceases and religion is devoted exclusively to Allah, while granting cessation if the enemy relents.

2:191-193: “And slay them wherever you come upon them, and expel them from where they expelled you; persecution is more grievous than slaying. But fight them not by the Holy Mosque until they should fight you there; then, if they fight you, slay them — such is the recompense of unbelievers, but if they give over, surely Allah is All-forgiving, All-compassionate. Fight them, till there is no persecution and the religion is Allah’s; then if they give over, there shall be no enmity save for evildoers.”   

- Compares wives to fields of cultivation that husbands may enter however they choose, paired with an injunction to fear Allah and perform righteous deeds.

2:223: "Your wives are a place of sowing of seed for you, so come to your place of cultivation however you wish and put forth [righteousness] for yourselves. And fear Allah and know that you will meet Him. And give good tidings to the believers"   

- Demands obedience to Allah and His messenger, declaring that Allah has no love for those who turn away in disbelief.

3:32: "Say, "Obey Allah and the Messenger." But if they turn away - then indeed, Allah does not like the disbelievers."

- Declares that terror will be struck into the hearts of polytheists for worshiping other entities without divine sanction, consigning them to Hell.

3:151: "We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve for what they have associated with Allah of which He had not sent down [any] authority. And their refuge will be the Fire, and wretched is the residence of the wrongdoers."

- Permits men to marry up to four women, or restrict themselves to one wife or enslaved concubines if they fear they cannot treat multiple wives equitably.

4:3: "And if you fear that you shall not be able to deal justly with the orphan girls, then marry (other) women of your choice, two or three, or four but if you fear that you shall not be able to deal justly (with them), then only one or (the captives and the slaves) that your right hands possess. That is nearer to prevent you from doing injustice."   

- Prohibits marriage to women who are already married, with an explicit exception made for female captives/enslaved women owned by believers.

4:24: "You are forbidden to marry married women except your slave-girls. This is the decree of God. Besides these, it is lawful for you to marry other women if you pay their dower, maintain chastity and do not commit indecency. If you marry them for the appointed time you must pay their dowries. There is no harm if you reach an understanding among yourselves about the dowry, God is all-knowing and all-wise."   

- Asserts male authority and maintenance over wives, and prescribes a three-step escalation for defiant wives: verbal admonishment, abandonment in bed, and physical striking.

4:34: "Men are in charge of women by [right of] what Allah has given one over the other and what they spend [for maintenance] from their wealth. So righteous women are devoutly obedient, guarding in [the husband's] absence what Allah would have them guard. But those [wives] from whom you fear arrogance - [first] advise them; [then if they persist], forsake them in bed; and [finally], beat them. But if they obey you [once more], seek no means against them. Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted and Grand."   

- States that disbelievers will be driven into hellfire, where their burned skins will be perpetually replaced with fresh skin to prolong their punishment.

4:56: "Indeed, those who disbelieve in our verses - We will drive them into a fire. Every time their skins are roasted through We will replace them with other skins so they may taste the punishment. Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted in Might and Wise."   

- Warns against allying with disbelievers who wish for Muslims to apostatize, commanding believers to capture and kill any who turn back or refuse to emigrate.

4:89: "They wish you would disbelieve as they disbelieved so you would be alike. So do not take from among them allies until they emigrate for the cause of Allah. But if they turn away, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them and take not from among them any ally or helper."   

- Grants explicit authorization to seize and execute duplicitous individuals who refuse to offer peace or withhold hostility from the believers.

4:91: "You will find others who wish to obtain security from you and [to] obtain security from their people. Every time they are returned to [the influence of] disbelief, they fall back into it. So if they do not withdraw from you or offer you peace or restrain their hands, then seize them and kill them wherever you overtake them. And those - We have made for you against them a clear authorization"   

- Prescribes execution, crucifixion, amputation of alternating hands and feet, or exile for those who wage war against Allah and His messenger and spread corruption.

5:33: “This is the recompense of those who fight against Allah and His Messenger, and hasten about the earth, to do corruption there: they shall be slaughtered, or crucified, or their hands and feet shall alternately be struck off; or they shall be banished from the land. That is a degradation for them in this world; and in the world to come awaits them a mighty chastisement.”   

- Forbids taking Jews and Christians as allies, warning that any believer who forms such an alliance is regarded as one of them.

5:51: "O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are [in fact] allies of one another. And whoever is an ally to them among you – then indeed, he is [one] of them. Indeed, Allah guides not the wrongdoing people."   

- Asserts that many jinn and humans were created specifically for Hell, describing them as spiritually obtuse, uncomprehending, and worse than livestock.

7:179: "And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind. They have hearts with which they do not understand, they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear. Those are like livestock; rather, they are more astray. It is they who are the heedless."

- Instructs angelic forces to strike fear into unbelievers and physically strike their necks and fingertips during battle.

8:12: “When thy Lord was revealing to the angels, ‘I am with you; so confirm the believers. I shall cast into the unbelievers’ hearts terror; so smite above the necks, and smite every finger of them!”

- Directs warfare against opponents until all fitnah (persecution/strife) is eliminated and religious obedience belongs solely to Allah.

8:39: "And fight them until there is no fitnah and [until] the religion, all of it, is for Allah. And if they cease - then indeed, Allah is Seeing of what they do."

- Describes angels striking the faces and backs of disbelievers at the moment of death, consigning them to hellfire.

8:50: "And if you could but see when the angels take the souls of those who disbelieved... They are striking their faces and their backs and [saying], "Taste the punishment of the Burning Fire."

- Orders the hunting, capture, besieging, and killing of polytheists after sacred months expire, unless they convert, pray, and pay alms.

9:5: “Then, when the sacred months are drawn away, slay the idolaters wherever you find them, and take them, and confine them, and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush. But if they repent, and perform the prayer, and pay the alms, then let them go their way; Allah is All-forgiving, All-compassionate.”

- Declares polytheists ritually impure and permanently bars them from entering the Sacred Mosque in Mecca.

9:28: "O you who have believed, indeed the polytheists [non-Muslims] are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-haram after this, their [final] year. And if you fear privation, Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Wise."

- Directs armed warfare against Jews and Christians who do not accept Islamic law until they pay tribute (jizya) in a state of submission.

9:29: “Fight those who believe not in Allah and the Last Day and do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden — such men as practice not the religion of truth, being of those who have been given the Book — until they pay the tribute out of hand and have been humbled.”

- Commands the Prophet to wage harsh combat against disbelievers and hypocrites, warning them of destination in Hell.

9:73: "O Prophet, fight against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh upon them. And their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination"

- Asserts that Allah has traded Paradise to believers in exchange for their lives and property spent fighting, killing, and being killed in His cause.

9:111: “Allah has bought from the believers their selves and their possessions against the gift of Paradise; they fight in the way of Allah; they kill, and are killed; that is a promise binding upon Allah in the Torah, and the Gospel, and the Koran; and who fulfils his covenant truer than Allah? So rejoice in the bargain you have made with Him; that is the mighty triumph.”   

- Commands believers to fight adjacent unbelievers with visible harshness.

9:123: “O believers, fight the unbelievers who are near to you; and let them find in you a harshness; and know that Allah is with the godfearing.”

- Details graphic punishments in the afterlife for disbelievers, including garments of fire, boiling liquids melting their flesh and organs, and iron hooked rods to push them back into torment.

22:19-22: "These twain (the believers and the disbelievers) are two opponents who contend concerning their Lord. But as for those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be cut out for them; boiling fluid will be poured down on their heads, Whereby that which is in their bellies, and their skins too, will be melted; And for them are hooked rods of iron. Whenever, in their anguish, they would go forth from thence they are driven back therein and (it is said unto them): Taste the doom of burning."   

- Instructs fighters to decapitate enemies in battle and take captives only after extensive slaughter, while promising divine reward to those slain in battle.

47:4: “When you meet the unbelievers, smite their necks, then, when you have made wide slaughter among them, tie fast the bonds; then set them free, either by grace or ransom, till the war lays down its loads. So it shall be; and if Allah had willed, He would have avenged Himself upon them; but that He may try some of you by means of others. And those who are slain in the way of Allah, He will not send their works astray.”   

- Describes Muhammad's followers as unyielding and fierce toward non-believers, but compassionate and gentle toward one another.

48:29: "Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah ; and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves..."

- Forbids seeking peace treaties when holding military superiority over the adversary.

47:35: "So do not weaken and call for peace while you are superior; and Allah is with you and will never deprive you of [the reward of] your deeds."

- Recounts the expulsion of the Jewish tribe of Banu Nadir, attributing their defeat to divine terror cast into their hearts that caused the destruction of their homes.

59:2: "It is He who expelled the ones who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering. You did not think they would leave, and they thought that their fortresses would protect them from Allah ; but [the decree of] Allah came upon them from where they had not expected, and He cast terror into their hearts [so] they destroyed their houses by their [own] hands and the hands of the believers. So take warning, O people of vision."   

- Declares polytheists and disbelieving People of the Book to be the worst of creation, doomed to eternal damnation in Hell.

98:6: "Indeed, they who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein. Those are the worst of creatures."

text:
Lately, I’ve had quite a few conversations with people who ask me the same question: “With so many alternative education programs opening across South Florida, aren’t you worried about the competition?”

It’s a fair question. Especially when you consider the challenges we’re facing with declining student enrollment, economic uncertainty, and an increasingly competitive educational landscape.

But my answer is always the same: Absolutely not.

I embrace competition. In fact, I welcome it.

Competition challenges me to think bigger, innovate, improve, and continuously raise the standards of what we offer families. It pushes me to become a better educator, entrepreneur, and leader.

I believe that as leaders in education, we have a responsibility to push boundaries, challenge traditional models, and earn the trust of parents through our actions, results, and commitment to their children.

Families deserve choices. They deserve transparency, accountability, and educational environments that genuinely meet their children’s needs.

The goal should never be to eliminate competition. It should be to become better because of it.

And if the growth of alternative education in South Florida means more families have access to meaningful educational opportunities, then I consider that a win for all of us.

There is room for innovation, but there should never be room for complacency when it comes to educating children.

CHA @ LAL: Lean Charlotte +7.5: new Lakers absences and sharp money, but the line already moved

Verdict: Lean Charlotte +7.5 for a half unit. 

Walker Kessler's new absence weakens the Lakers where Charlotte is strongest, and the market has moved hard toward the Hornets, but that three-point move has already taken most of the value.

Picks
• CHA +7.5 -110 (Hard Rock Bet) · 0.5u

Two Lakers starters who are not in the recent numbers are out tonight. Walker Kessler (C) played Nov 15 and had started all 14 games, so his 10.9 rebounds a game (27% of the Lakers' boards) are missing from every recent split. Austin Reaves (G) scores 24.7 points (20% of team points) and has missed only the Phoenix game. The Lakers are 2-0 without Reaves, but they have never played a game without Kessler this season. Charlotte has been without Kon Knueppel (G) and Dennis Schroder (G) since Nov 8, so those losses are already in its recent form. Its -10.8 season margin barely changed with or without Schroder.

Kessler's absence hits the unit where Charlotte is elite. The Hornets rebound 33.1% of their own misses, second in the league, and the Lakers already ranked 28th in defensive rebounding (68.4%) with him. Charlotte also takes 44.8 threes a game (#1) against a defense that allows 40.9 attempts (27th) at 36.6% (23rd). That is a high-variance shot profile, which helps an underdog. On the road the Hornets lose by an average of 6.7 points (n=6), against 14.3 at home. The real weakness is ball security. Charlotte commits 19.4 turnovers a game (#30), and the Lakers lead the league in steals at 11.0. The Hornets gave it away 27 times at Phoenix on Nov 12 and still covered +6.5.

The market agrees with the injury read. The spread opened LAL -10.5 and sits at -7.5 even though the Lakers have 85% of tickets and 77% of the money. The moneyline went from -451 to -296. Pinnacle has backed Charlotte all pre-game, moving from +9 to +7. Your systems line up on the same side: seven of them back Charlotte at +6.5, with a median 55% hit rate and +4.7% ROI, and the top two hit 63% and 61%. Only six fire on the Lakers.

The price is the catch. At Pinnacle's +7 -101, CHA +7.5 (-110 Hard Rock Bet) grades out slightly negative (-3.0% EV at the best price). The three-point move has already absorbed most of the injury edge.

The quarter markets do not offer a cleaner angle. The Lakers score 31.7 first-quarter points (#1) against Charlotte's 24.8 (#29), which rules out early Hornets plays. Charlotte's 21.1 fourth-quarter points (#30) argue against CHA +2.5 (-106 FanDuel) in the second half. The full game is the only market where your systems, the reverse move and the rebounding mismatch all point the same way.

The best case for the Lakers: they have the league's top offense (121.2 per 100), Luka Doncic (G) just scored 43, they have won 8 straight and they are 10-4 ATS. Charlotte's offense (100.3) is the league's worst.

That keeps this to a half-unit lean on CHA +7.5 (-110 Hard Rock Bet) at Hard Rock's -110, well below the -119 consensus. If you want a safer leg for a combo, CHA +8.5 (-130 ESPN BET) buys the extra point.

text:
The $NVDA  beat is the least interesting number in this report. The lender of last resort is the story, and neocloud shareholders hold the risk.

Here is my thesis, stated plainly. NVIDIA's third quarter was excellent, but anyone who stops at the beat is reading the wrong page. The page that matters is the CFO commentary, which shows how far NVIDIA has become the financing backstop for the neocloud industry, and how conditionally that backstop is written, so that the first losses fall on someone else. If I am right, the market is debating whether AI demand is real when it should be debating who owns the funding risk. I think the answer is the neocloud equity.

The quarter, briefly

NVIDIA reported revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year ago, against an LSEG consensus of about $109.1 billion. Adjusted EPS was $2.68 against $2.48. Data Center revenue was $107.6 billion, up 110%, against roughly $101.9 billion expected by StreetAccount. Fourth-quarter revenue is guided to $130.0 billion, plus or minus 3%, versus a consensus near $125.1 billion, with no Data Center compute revenue from China assumed, and interim CEO Colette Kress raised the fiscal 2028 growth outlook to about 75% from 70%. Gross margin is guided to 71% to 72%, down from 74.9% this quarter. In extended trading the stock was up about 4% as of ~18:40 ET, after closing at $155.46 and falling about 24% for the month. That is a measured reaction to a beat this size: the market already knew demand was strong and was worried about something else.

Demand is not the question

The bulls are right about demand. The AI Clouds, Industrial and Enterprise platform, where the neoclouds sit, grew 195% to $47.5 billion, nearly tripling in a year, while Hyperscale grew 71% to $60.1 billion. Vera Rubin NVL72 has shipped, and NVIDIA has said racks are running at partners including CoreWeave and Nebius. But that answers a question nobody is asking. Few doubt these companies can rent out GPUs. The doubt is whether they can finance the buildings, the power and the chips to do so at a cost their revenue can carry. Demand is necessary and it is not sufficient. CoreWeave grew third-quarter revenue 168% and still lost $709 million after $846 million of net interest expense. Growth bought with debt that must keep being refinanced does not make a safe equity.

Read what NVIDIA actually wrote

Start with the size. NVIDIA discloses up to $32 billion of neocloud agreements, formerly labelled AI cloud agreements, running through fiscal 2032 and thereafter, with nothing in the remainder of fiscal 2027 and $6 billion in fiscal 2028. That maximum is less than a third of a single quarter of NVIDIA revenue, spread over five fiscal years. Then read the condition. By NVIDIA's own wording, these commitments take effect only if the neocloud secures financing to buy the infrastructure and the capacity is deployed, made operational and accepted by NVIDIA. If those contingencies are not timely resolved, the amount and timing of the commitments may be affected, and certain commitments could be reduced or eliminated. In exchange, NVIDIA earns revenue on the upfront hardware sale and, if criteria are met, a share of the neocloud's revenue from its customers.

Now the guarantees. Total maximum gross exposure is $118 billion: $105 billion of credit support for SB Energy's Ohio campus, which will host NVIDIA infrastructure under 20-year leases to OpenAI, plus $9.5 billion of power and systems credit support and the neocloud guarantees below. These guarantees take effect building by building, the first is expected in fiscal 2029, and the exposure peaks at $105 billion and then declines over each 20-year lease. The land, power and shell guarantees for neoclouds are $3.5 billion, about 3% of the total. NVIDIA says it has made no payments under any guarantee. Meanwhile, NVIDIA says many neoclouds are growing faster than their balance sheets and long-term credit profiles can support, and that it will focus on exceptional sites where visible, durable demand can support multiple generations of its compute.

Put those facts together. NVIDIA is not extending support freely to the neocloud sector. It is rationing it, directing the largest guarantee to a single OpenAI-leased campus, and making its smaller neocloud commitments conditional on the neocloud first raising money from someone else. A careful lender of last resort behaves exactly this way, and it protects NVIDIA's own shareholders. It is also the reason I do not think the neocloud equity can lean on the backstop the way the market has assumed. The backstop is a selection mechanism, and the neocloud still has to clear the lenders first.

The bears have the right worry and the wrong target

The bear case is circular financing: NVIDIA funds its customers, who buy NVIDIA chips, and the loop breaks when a link fails. I think this misreads the balance sheet. NVIDIA generated $43.8 billion of free cash flow in the quarter and returned $28.1 billion to shareholders, with $227.3 billion left on its buyback authorization. Its guarantees are phased, contingent on partner default, and NVIDIA has made no payments under them to date. The gross figure sounds frightening, but I do not see NVIDIA's balance sheet as the weak link, though the scale is not trivial: cash and marketable securities were $53.5 billion, against $518 billion of total future commitments plus $32 billion of neocloud agreements and $118 billion of maximum guarantee exposure. There are flags, and I will name them: days sales outstanding rose to 64 from 60, which NVIDIA attributes to shipment linearity from the Rubin launch and extended payment terms on large multi-quarter agreements with certain investment-grade customers, and NVIDIA recorded a $1.0 billion net loss on non-marketable equity securities, including a $1.8 billion impairment, against $2.8 billion of gains on publicly held securities. Neither is alarming, but both are worth watching as NVIDIA takes on more customer exposure.

So the circularity risk is real, but it does not sit mainly with NVIDIA. If a neocloud cannot close its financing, NVIDIA's commitment simply does not take effect. NVIDIA loses a customer and a revenue share. The neocloud's shareholders lose the project. The risk is not circular. It is asymmetric, and it runs downhill.

The neocloud numbers, from company reports

I would not call these companies weak. I would call them highly levered to a funding window. As reported, CoreWeave guided 2026 revenue to $13.0 billion to $13.3 billion, reported a $132.5 billion backlog, and guided capex to $37 billion to $39 billion, roughly three times its revenue guide, and, as noted, it posted a $709 million net loss in the quarter. NVIDIA is a large CoreWeave shareholder. Nebius reported 571% revenue growth to $980.8 million, including about $325 million of non-recurring revenue from its asset-light model, yet guided to the low end of its $3.0 billion to $3.4 billion 2026 range on delays tied to third-party data center capacity. Those are company-reported figures from CoreWeave's November 10 and Nebius's November 12 earnings releases. The Nebius delay is the telling detail. The constraint on that business was not chip demand. It was the physical site, which is exactly the land, power and shell problem NVIDIA says is the next critical phase.

Apollo CEO Marc Rowan told CNBC on Tuesday that "if that banking function, that guarantor function, gets taken away, access to capital for a large number of neoclouds is going to disappear." Apollo is itself one of NVIDIA's six financing partners. He also expects financial innovation to follow, in the way finance arms grew up around the first automakers. Mizuho wrote on Sunday that Jensen Huang was viewed as the global dealmaker and 'AI banker'. CNBC reports that Huang has said he is open to returning, and that board chair Harvey Jones says the board does not intend to bring him back as CEO, with a search under way. I only note that the funding function the market worries about was closely tied to a founder, and the company is now run by an interim CEO. Fortune also noted media reports that Kress, and Huang before his exit, were rethinking NVIDIA's role as the industry's central bank.

The tape, with a caveat

In extended trading as of ~18:40 ET, $NBIS was up about 10.6%, $APLD about 9.4%, $IREN about 9.2%, $CIFR about 8.9%, $CRWV about 8.5% and $WULF about 7.8%, with $ORCL up about 4.2% as a hyperscale comparison. Early reports had many of these in the single digits, and the moves widened later in the session, when extended-hours volume is thin. CNBC noted that CoreWeave and Nebius were each down more than 50% over the last three months. Read these as relief that demand held, not an answer on funding. NVIDIA's commentary did not resolve the funding question.

What would prove me wrong

I want to be specific, because a thesis that cannot lose is not worth publishing. I am wrong if neoclouds close the financing that triggers NVIDIA's commitments, and do so at costs that fall rather than rise. CoreWeave's 9.75% bonds due 2031 were yielding 15.66% on Tuesday, per CNBC, so falling yields would be the clearest signal. I am wrong if the asset managers NVIDIA partnered with in August, Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR, keep deploying capital through the $500 billion financing platforms without NVIDIA's residual-value support behind it. And I am wrong if NVIDIA's next CEO widens its support for neoclouds rather than narrowing it. Any of these would say the backstop is becoming a durable market, not a rationed favor.

My view, and a question

Strong results and a hungry market have made the neocloud trade look like a bet on demand. I think it is a bet on credit, and the party best placed to see that is the one that wrote the commitments with conditions attached. None of this is investment advice, and I am sharing my reading of public filings and reports.

My question for anyone who disagrees: if NVIDIA's support were limited to what is already written down, which neocloud has a funding plan that works, and what is your evidence for it?

The FCAS collapse offers India a crucial lesson. Divided design authority, competing industrial interests and poorly structured partnerships can derail even ambitious fighter programs.

France's roadmap:
🔹 2035: Evolved Rafale F5.
🔹 2045: New combat aircraft program, with a demonstrator already under conception.

What should India do?

🔹 Tejas Mk2: Expedite development, target first flight in 2027–28 and induction in the early-to-mid 2030s. This must become the foundation of our indigenous medium-weight fighter ecosystem.

🔹 TEDBF: Stop delaying its sanction. Expedite development, parallelise prototyping and testing, and target induction by 2038. The Navy cannot keep depending on foreign platforms for carrier aviation.

🔹 ORCA: Develop it as a land-based derivative of TEDBF, leveraging common systems, propulsion and design architecture wherever feasible. Build a family of fighters rather than isolated platforms.

🔹 AMCA: Give a single lead integrator clear design authority, accountability and execution autonomy. Target first flight by 2029–30 and induction in the late 2030s, subject to development realities.

🔹 Indigenous engines: Launch a fully funded parallel indigenous turbofan program. No sovereign sixth-generation fighter is possible without sovereign propulsion.

🔹 Sixth generation: Start a national technology demonstrator by 2035, targeting an operational platform in the 2045–50 timeframe. Invest now in adaptive-cycle engines, advanced stealth, AI-enabled sensor fusion, CCA, directed energy and collaborative combat architectures.

And why Rafale Make in India or joining FCAS?

Rafale is a mature 4.5-generation design, not a clean-sheet next-generation platform. Its F5 upgrade will extend its relevance, but expensive licensed production does not automatically give India sovereign design authority or control over critical IP.

Rather than commit enormous resources to Rafale assembly, buy 2-3 squadrons of Rafale off the shelf and invest the savings in the Tejas Mk2 → TEDBF → ORCA pathway.

The twin-engine TEDBF architecture offers greater aggregate thrust potential through two F414-class engines, while the indigenous development pathway creates opportunities to own and continuously upgrade the aircraft's design, systems and technologies and propulsion.

Our objective should be to build platforms that can eventually match and surpass imported fighters across critical capability parameters, not merely assemble them.

The real strategic advantage is IP ownership: the freedom to integrate new engines, radars, EW systems, weapons, software and sensors throughout the aircraft's service life without seeking another country's permission.

AMCA must not be our destination. It must be the stepping stone towards India's own sixth-generation combat aviation ecosystem.

Don't buy another generation of dependency. Build the capability to own every generation that follows.

OCHA’s Financial Tracking Service (FTS)—managed centrally out of OCHA’s Financing and Outreach Division in Istanbul—serves as the humanitarian system's primary public ledger for tracking resource flows and calculating funding deficits. To monitor both bilateral (direct donor-to-agency/NGO) and pooled (CERF and Country-Based Pooled Funds) contributions without double-counting, FTS relies on a relational flow-accounting architecture paired with automated pooled-fund data pipelines.

As of mid-November 2026, FTS tracks $23.2 billion in total global humanitarian funding reported across the year, benchmarking incoming resources against Inter-Agency Standing Committee (IASC) coordinated requirements.

1. The FTS Relational "Flow Model" and Boundary Accounting

Introduced to prevent cascading pass-through grants from inflating headline totals, the FTS Flow Model records every reported financial or in-kind transaction as a discrete node ("flow") linked in parent-child chains from original source to field implementer.

Boundary Classification (Incoming vs. Internal vs. Outgoing): Rather than relying on static spreadsheet totals, FTS dynamically draws analytical "boundaries" around user-defined parameters (e.g., Affected Country + Year, Humanitarian Response Plan [HRP], or Specific Cluster).
Incoming Flows: Contributions crossing into the defined boundary from an external source (e.g., a Member State funding an HRP project or a previous-year carry-over). Only incoming flows count toward closing a plan’s funding gap.
Internal Flows: Secondary pass-throughs or reallocations originating and terminating inside the same boundary (e.g., a UN agency sub-granting bilateral funds to an implementing NGO). FTS links these as child flows to preserve downstream visibility while strictly excluding them from top-line sums to eliminate double-counting.
Outgoing Flows: Unspent funds carried forward into a subsequent calendar year or transferred outside the boundary.

Commitment Thresholds (Pledges vs. Commitments/Paid): FTS logs verbal or conference pledges in a separate transparency register for follow-up, but excludes them from gap calculations until a legally binding agreement (commitment) is signed or funds are transferred (paid contribution).
2. Differentiated Ingestion Pipelines: Bilateral vs. Pooled Funds
FTS ingests data through distinct reporting pathways depending on whether funding moves bilaterally or through multilateral pooled mechanisms:
Funding ModalityIngestion Mechanism & Source SystemGranularity & Verification ProtocolBilateral ContributionsVoluntary reporting via FTS Standard Reporting Templates, HQ focal points (UN agencies, OECD DAC donors, Red Cross/Red Crescent, private sector), and OCHA field offices.Triangulated & Curation-Validated: FTS curators cross-check donor reports against recipient agency reports to reconcile currency conversions, earmarking levels, and destination clusters before publication.Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF)Direct integration with the CERF Secretariat and the UNDP Multi-Partner Trust Fund (MPTF) Office gateway.Automated Parent-Child Linking: Tracks donor contributions into the global CERF pool separately from outgoing Rapid Response / Underfunded Emergency grants to UN agencies (and NGO pass-throughs) to prevent double-counting at the global vs. country boundary.Country-Based Pooled Funds (CBPFs)Direct API/report export from OCHA’s Grant Management System (GMS) (via GMS FTS Reports) and OCHA's Country-Based Pooled Funds Section (CBPFS).Project-Level Mapping: Automatically links donor deposits into a country fund (e.g., DRC or Afghanistan Humanitarian Funds) with downstream GMS project disbursements to national/international NGOs, UN agencies, and Red Cross societies.

3. Calculating Funding Gaps: "Inside" vs. "Outside" Response Plans

A critical analytical distinction in FTS is how it isolates unmet appeal requirements from broader humanitarian spending in a crisis-affected country:

Requirement Baselines (HPC Integration): FTS pulls financial requirements directly from OCHA’s Humanitarian Programme Cycle (HPC) tools—specifically the Project Module (PM) and Response Planning Module (RPM). Every project uploaded into a Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) or Flash Appeal establishes the denominator for country-level and sector/cluster-level funding requirements.

Boundary Filtering (Inside Plan vs. Outside Plan):
Coordinated Plan Coverage (Gap Calculation): When evaluating an appeal page, FTS filters strictly for incoming flows explicitly mapped to approved HRP/Flash Appeal projects. Subtracting mapped incoming commitments/paid contributions from total plan requirements yields the official funding gap and percentage coverage per cluster (e.g., Health, Food Security, Protection).
Outside-Plan Flows: Bilateral donations to non-appeal actors (such as certain Red Cross movements, bilateral government-to-government aid, or NGO programs outside the HRP) are captured on the Affected Country Page as total humanitarian assistance to the country, but are segregated from the HRP coverage ratio so they do not artificially mask unfunded coordinated appeal deficits.
4. Structural Blind Spots and Analytical Limitations
While FTS provides the authoritative real-time baseline for humanitarian advocacy and CERF Underfunded Emergency (UFE) allocation modeling, practitioners account for four structural blind spots:
Voluntary Reporting Asymmetry: Because reporting is voluntary rather than legally mandated, bilateral contributions from non-DAC donors, Gulf states, private foundations, and direct grants to local/national NGOs are frequently underreported or logged with significant time lags compared to UN agency and GMS pooled-fund feeds.
Unspecified Cluster Attribution: Bilateral donors frequently report large, unearmarked or softly earmarked commitments to a UN agency at the country level without specifying a target sector. Until OCHA Country Offices manually trace and verify downstream allocations with the recipient agency, those funds appear as "Cluster Not Yet Specified," temporarily inflating apparent sector-level gaps.
Multi-Year & Sub-Granting Opacity: Multi-year bilateral pledges require annual tranche splitting to align with single-year HRP boundaries. Additionally, while GMS provides full visibility into CBPF sub-grants to national NGOs, downstream sub-granting of bilateral funds from UN agencies to local partners remains inconsistently reported as child flows.
In-Kind Valuation Variance: In-kind bilateral contributions (such as airlifted medical supplies or food commodities) rely on donor-declared valuations, which may include domestic procurement markups and logistics overhead that do not directly offset cash-denominated HRP project budgets.
----------------
As of mid-November 2026, OCHA’s Financial Tracking Service (FTS) data across the 2026 Global Humanitarian Overview (GHO) reveals a stark structural divergence in how donor capital is distributed across Food Security, Health, and Protection.

While Food Security commands the largest absolute dollar volume, it suffers from the steepest nominal funding deficit and ranks well below the GHO system-wide coverage average (44.9%). Conversely, core Protection exhibits a sharp internal bifurcation between general Protection (70.0% covered) and specialized sub-sectors such as Gender-Based Violence (30.4%) and Child Protection (36.3%). Health captures the second-largest total funding envelope across all humanitarian sectors ($2.56 billion reported globally), propelled heavily by acute epidemic emergencies such as the DRC Bundibugyo Ebola response and cholera outbreaks.

1. Comparative Sectoral Overview (FTS 2026 Data)

In FTS global sector accounting, total reported humanitarian funding is divided between flows mapped inside GHO coordinated plans (which count toward appeal coverage) and outside-plan flows (bilateral or Red Cross/Red Crescent assistance outside formal UN appeals):

Global Sector / Area of Responsibility (AoR)Total FTS Funding (US$M)Funding Inside GHO Plans (USM)∣FundingOutsidePlans(USM)2026 GHO Requirements (USM)∣GHOCoverage(%)∣UnmetGHOGap(USM)Food Security$4,836.0*$3,492.9$748.5Health$2,564.2— (see note)— (see note)Protection (General)$1,595.9$1,174.9$421.1Protection – Child Protection$325.3$252.4$72.9Protection – Gender-Based Violence (GBV)$215.0$171.5$43.4Protection – Housing, Land & Property (HLP)$24.7$19.5$5.2
*Note on FTS Reporting Lags & Attribution: Food Security’s GHO plan breakdown ($3,492.9M inside plans / $9,470.0M required) reflects the November 3, 2026 sector snapshot, while its headline total ($4,836.0M) reflects the November 15, 2026 Global Sector Overview update. Additionally, across all GHO plans, $2,764.7 million (17.5% of tracked GHO funding) and $603.2 million in multi-cluster grants remain categorized as "Not Specified" or "Shared" pending downstream agency sub-allocation—meaning final year-end sector coverage rates for Health, Food Security, and Protection will adjust upward once UN agencies report sub-allocations.
2. Sector-by-Sector Analytical Breakdown
1. Food Security: Highest Dollar Demand, Largest Nominal Deficit
Scale of Contraction: Representing roughly 27% of all 2026 GHO financial requirements ($9.47 billion), Food Security remains the single largest pillar of the global humanitarian appeal. However, total reported Food Security funding ($4.24B–$4.84B) has contracted by more than 62% from its 2022 peak of $12.9 billion (and down from $10.0B in 2024 and $6.2B in 2025).
Coverage Deficit & Operational Triage: At 36.9% coverage, Food Security trails the overall GHO average (44.9%) by 8 percentage points, leaving a $5.98 billion shortfall. Because needs are concentrated in active famine or IPC Phase 5 zones—most notably the Occupied Palestinian Territory, Sudan, DRC, Ethiopia, Ukraine, Haiti, Syria, Bangladesh, Kenya, and Yemen—agencies like WFP and FAO have been forced into severe rationing (such as halving hot meal distributions in Gaza) and cutting agricultural resilience programming.
2. Health: Second-Largest Global Volume Driven by Epidemic Surges
Capital Concentration: With $2,564.2 million in total reported funding as of November 15, 2026, Health is the second-largest sector in the humanitarian system by dollar volume, trailing only Food Security.
Structural Drivers: Unlike sectors reliant primarily on long-term baseline grants, 2026 Health inflows have been buoyed by acute infectious disease emergencies and infrastructure collapse—specifically the Bundibugyo Ebola PHEIC in the DRC, large-scale cholera outbreaks in Yemen (339,000+ suspected cases) and Somalia, hospital destruction in Gaza and Sudan (where up to 80% of facilities are non-functional), and trauma care in Ukraine and Haiti. Within WHO’s dedicated $1 billion 2026 emergency health appeal framework, donor disbursements prioritize epidemic containment, cold-chain biologics, and emergency trauma kits, leaving chronic maternal, mental health, and non-communicable disease services severely under-resourced.
3. Protection: High Core Coverage vs. Severe Sub-Sector Underfunding
The General Protection Anomaly (70.0%): General Protection appears substantially better funded than Food Security or the GHO average, reaching 70.0% coverage ($1,174.9 million funded against $1,678.4 million required). Two structural factors explain this high ratio:
Denominator Compression: During the 2026 hyper-prioritization exercise, Protection clusters sharply narrowed appeal budgets to core legal aid, displacement monitoring, and civilian protection in high-visibility conflicts—led by Ukraine, Syria, Occupied Palestinian Territory, Colombia, Afghanistan, Lebanon, and Sudan.
UNHCR Earmarking: Core refugee and IDP protection envelopes benefit from sustained multi-year institutional support channeled through UNHCR.
Specialized Area of Responsibility (AoR) Collapse: When disaggregated into specialized Protection sub-sectors, coverage drops precipitously:
Gender-Based Violence (GBV): Only 30.4% funded ($171.5 million of $564.5 million required), leaving a $393.0 million gap.
Child Protection: Only 36.3% funded ($252.4 million of $694.8 million required), leaving a $442.4 million gap.
Mine Action: $267.4 million reported globally, concentrated heavily in Ukraine, Syria, and Afghanistan.
3. Cross-Sectoral Structural Takeaways
Tangible Life-Saving Bias vs. Preventive Services: When donor budgets contract, funding gravitates toward immediate, quantifiable commodity and clinical interventions (food rations, epidemic containment, emergency shelter) while preventive and community-based services (GBV case management, Child Protection safe spaces, and FAO agricultural livelihood inputs—where Agriculture sits at just $67.6 million globally) absorb disproportionate cuts.
High Outside-Plan Ratios in Health and Protection: Roughly 26.4% of total Protection funding ($421.1M of $1,595.9M) is channeled outside formal GHO coordinated plans—a significantly higher outside-plan share than Food Security (15.5%)—reflecting substantial bilateral funding to the ICRC/Red Cross movement, international human rights/legal NGOs, and domestic refugee-hosting ministries.
-------------------------
Within the 2026 humanitarian architecture tracked by OCHA’s Financial Tracking Service (FTS) and global Global Humanitarian Overview (GHO) plans, Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) faces some of the most severe underfunding and structural delivery bottlenecks of any operational sector.

While sectors like Food Security and Health command massive centralized emergency mobilization, WASH operations are disproportionately impacted by capital scarcity, hardware import restrictions, and infrastructure destruction—triggering compounding public health crises such as acute watery diarrhea (AWD), cholera outbreaks, and severe water insecurity in theaters like Gaza, Yemen, and the DRC.

1. 2026 WASH Funding Deficits and Global Gaps

WASH appeal coverage within 2026 GHO plans consistently lags behind system-wide recovery averages, with acute geographic disparities:

Extreme Underfunding in Protracted Crises: In high-intensity or neglected contexts, WASH funding deficits severely constrain preventive health. For instance, UNICEF and WASH Cluster data for Yemen revealed that out of 14.4 million people requiring urgent WASH assistance, only 14% of the required $178.7 million was funded mid-year, leaving millions dependent on malfunctioning piped networks or expensive private water trucking.

Capital Intensity vs. Short-Term Disbursal: Unlike cash-transfer modalities or bulk food distributions that can be scaled rapidly through UN common pipelines, WASH requires capital-intensive physical infrastructure (solar-powered boreholes, wastewater treatment plants, piped networks, and prefab sanitation modules). When donor funding contracts or arrives late in erratic tranches, WASH actors are forced to abandon sustainable infrastructure rehabilitation in favor of temporary, high-per-capita emergency fixes like water trucking.
The "Dual-Use" Vetting Bottleneck: In high-conflict settings like the Occupied Palestinian Territory, critical WASH commodities—including water pumps, chlorine disinfection supplies, generator spare parts, pipes, and wastewater clearing machinery—are frequently classified under restrictive "dual-use" import lists. These items face prolonged administrative vetting, inspection delays, or outright bans, leaving millions facing high rates of water insecurity (such as over 42% of households experiencing moderate-to-severe water insecurity in Gaza alongside flooded seasonal latrines).
2. Core Operational Bottlenecks in 2026 WASH Responses

Cross-analysing recent regional WASH Cluster reports and operational evaluations highlights four systemic bottlenecks crippling emergency response delivery:

Operational BottleneckRoot Cause & MechanismHumanitarian ConsequenceSupply Chain & Import RestrictionsBureaucratic vetting of "dual-use" mechanical and chemical inputs (chlorine, pumps, pipes, heavy excavation gear).Inability to repair bombed or overloaded municipal water networks; reliance on fragile, high-cost water trucking.Fuel & Energy DeficitsChronic fuel shortages and grid destruction disabling municipal water-treatment plants and borehole pumps.Complete cessation of piped municipal water, forcing populations to consume unsafe surface water or brackish sources.Insecurity & Access DenialsActive combat zones, restricted humanitarian corridors, and bureaucratic movement permits preventing technical teams from reaching damaged infrastructure.Prolonged outage of sanitation facilities in displacement camps, sharply increasing risks of waterborne disease outbreaks (cholera, AWD).Siloed Coordination & Funding TrapsDisconnection between short-term humanitarian emergency grants and long-term water sector capital development.Failure to transition temporary camp latrines and bladders into durable municipal systems during protracted displacement.

3. Public Health Intersections: WASH as the First Line of Defense against Epidemics
The compounding deficits in WASH funding directly exacerbate parallel health emergencies:
Cholera and AWD Amplification: In regions experiencing concurrent climate shocks and conflict—such as the DRC (where the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak coincides with strained sanitation infrastructure in Ituri) and Yemen—unfunded WASH appeals directly drive spikes in acute watery diarrhea and cholera. Without proper fecal sludge management and household water treatment chemicals, medical responses (such as Ebola treatment centers or oral rehydration points) are constantly overwhelmed by secondary waterborne disease loads.
Winterization Failures: As seen in Gaza and Afghanistan ahead of the 2026–2027 winter, heavy seasonal rains flooding makeshift tent sites without drainage or raised flooring destroy sanitation infrastructure, contaminating shallow groundwater tables and causing immediate spikes in skin infections, gastroenteritis, and respiratory illnesses among displaced children.

The enforcement of broad national security **"dual-use" import restrictions**—designating civilian equipment, chemicals, and mechanical parts as potential components for military or militant use—has emerged as one of the most severe regulatory bottlenecks governing Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) interventions in conflict-affected environments, most acutely in the Occupied Palestinian Territory (Gaza and the West Bank).

While designed to prevent the proliferation of weaponry or illicit infrastructure, these restrictions create severe operational, public health, and logistical friction.

---

### 1. Classification Mechanisms and the "Critical Humanitarian Items" Clash

Under standard international trade and non-proliferation frameworks (such as the Wassenaar Arrangement), dual-use lists govern chemicals, electronics, and heavy machinery with legitimate civilian applications that could be repurposed for military ends. In active conflict and occupied zones, however, these lists are unilaterally expanded by controlling authorities to encompass **Critical Humanitarian Items (CHIs)** essential for water and sanitation:

* **Restricted WASH Inputs:** Standard items routinely blocked or subjected to multi-month administrative vetting include heavy excavation and debris-removal machinery (needed to clear blocked sewer mains), water-pumping generators, solar-panel arrays, electrical inverters, submersible borehole pumps, wastewater treatment chemicals (such as chlorine gas and high-test hypochlorite), water-quality testing kits, and PVC/HDPE piping components.
* **Procedural Opacity:** Humanitarian organizations (including UNICEF, OCHA, and local water authorities) frequently face shifting, unpublished criteria without formal appeal mechanisms. Identical consignments approved in one inspection cycle are routinely rejected in another, leading to massive backlogs at border crossings and transit hubs.

---

### 2. Operational Impacts on WASH Infrastructure

When heavy machinery, electrical spares, and water treatment supplies are barred or delayed under dual-use rules, the physical water and sanitation architecture undergoes rapid, systemic degradation:

* **Paralysis of Wastewater Treatment:** In Gaza, where all municipal wastewater treatment plants and the vast majority of sewage pumping stations were rendered non-operational or severely damaged, restrictions on replacement pumps, electrical spares, and excavation gear prevent engineers from repairing ruptured mains. Consequently, over 150,000 cubic meters of raw sewage are discharged daily into streets, agricultural land, and coastal waters, contaminating shallow aquifers.
* **Forced Reliance on High-Cost, Fragile Alternatives:** Without imported spare parts to fix municipal desalination plants or deep borehole pumps, humanitarian actors are forced to rely on decentralized, low-capacity emergency measures—such as small mobile RO units and emergency water trucking. Water trucking requires unhindered fuel access and safe road conditions, both of which are simultaneously constrained by parallel security restrictions.
* **Degradation of Public Health Standards:** The inability to import water-treatment chemicals (chlorine and coagulants) prevents municipal facilities from maintaining safe residual disinfection levels. This immediately drives spikes in acute watery diarrhea (AWD), cholera, and hepatitis E, particularly in overcrowded displacement camps where sanitation facilities lack functioning drainage.

---

### 3. Legal and Regulatory Tensions under International Humanitarian Law (IHL)

Humanitarian legal analysts and human rights organizations (such as Gisha and international legal monitors) argue that applying expansive dual-use restrictions to basic water and sanitation equipment conflicts with binding legal obligations:

* **Obligations of Occupying Powers / Controlling Authorities:** Under Fourth Geneva Convention (GC IV, Article 55) and Customary International Humanitarian Law (ICRC Rule 55), authorities exercising effective control over a territory have an affirmative duty to ensure the population's survival supplies, including clean water, sanitation equipment, and medical infrastructure.
* **Proportionality and End-Use Monitoring Failures:** Legal frameworks permit vetting to verify that consignments do not contain contraband; however, legal experts argue that sweeping, blanket bans on fundamental water sanitation assets violate the principle of proportionality—weighing speculative, long-term security risks against the immediate, catastrophic public health collapse of an entire civilian population. Proposed reforms emphasize narrowing dual-use lists strictly to strategic military threats while pairing them with rigorous, transparent end-use monitoring (EUM) and pre-inspected humanitarian green-lanes.
